en: Abhidhānottara, Chapter 64: (The Unveiling of the Union of the Wrathful Lord Vajrabhairava). Now I shall explain the supreme yoga, which brings about the destruction of all that is evil, removes external and internal suffering, and is like the sky of emptiness.
Born from the syllable *kṣaḥ*, she is surrounded by a network of ḍākinīs;
she has two arms, one face, and three eyes, and is most terrifying.
She stands in the *ālīḍha* posture, treading upon the enemy Māra, the foe of the wicked.
Having entered into the Mahāmudrā, he embraces the bell within the skull-cup;
having placed the vajra-marked, supremely beautiful skull-cup in the center,
it is filled with the nectar of gnosis by his right hand.
Having a body of universal vajras, with a form marked by the six mudrās;
with a face terrifying with bared fangs, adorned with a crest of skulls;
with a head marked by a universal vajra, wearing matted locks and a crescent moon.
One should meditate on Vajrasattva as the crown [deity], [specifically] Vajrabhairava;
one whose fear is shattered, whose intellect is completely purified, and who has stilled all conceptualizations and afflictions.
His limbs adorned with the ornaments of loving-kindness and compassion,
the yogi free from attachment, his self firmly established in bliss,
[dwells] in the utterly inaccessible great charnel ground.
In a place where the cries of Vetālas and Rākṣasas are released, where the ground is strewn with the howling of jackals,
or elsewhere in a location suitable for the practitioner.
Alternatively, one should visualize this four-faced deity with eight arms,
white, blue, red, and yellow, with averted faces that are terrifying,
holding a trident, a vajra, a khaṭvāṅga, a ḍamaru, a severed head, and a curved knife.

With universal arms and a trembling tongue, resounding with the sounds "hā hā hīḥ hīḥ" and "phaṭ," the wise one should emanate clouds of wrathful deities through the yoga of body, speech, and mind— [deities] who are solitary heroes of terrifying form, subduers of all the most difficult to tame.
For the sake of accomplishing delight in meditative cultivation, one succeeds through the form of the Wrathful One.
One should recite within the consumption of the *samaya* substances; one should recite within the enclosure of the *samaya*;
one should recite by means of the summary of equanimity, through the cultivation of the dharma of equanimity.
Oṃ āḥ kṣaḥ hūṃ phaṭ.
"Bhūr bhuve" shall consume evil; it shall consume the five sins of immediate retribution.
It shall consume all sufferings and those things that must be purified from existence.
This most excellent yoga is supreme; when recited, it is certainly accomplished.
Those beings who are wicked and fierce, those who delight in cruel deeds,
and those ruined by false views— he certainly devours them;
yet he radiates an emanation of a flood of Buddhas and delivers the triple world.
One should recite the Lord of Mantras, the Leader of Mantras, together with its name:
*Oṃ phaṭ [Name] bhakṣaya phaṭ kṣaḥ hūṃ phaṭ*.
With a mind full of the wrath of Ādhmātaka, subsisting on a diet of flesh, one should remain naked.
With disheveled hair, mounted upon a corpse, and holding a noose and a goad in his hands,
one should recite the mantra according to the ritual rules while maintaining the visualization for ten thousand repetitions.
By means of this application of the ritual, one may destroy the triple world.
One should contemplate [him] being devoured by the retinue of ḍākinīs;
the wrathful one is made to enter the heart by those who have transformed themselves into vajra-needles,
[the heart] being torn open along with the marrow, bones, flesh, and blood.
One should slay the evil-minded ones who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution.
Having caused the ḍāka, joined with the ḍākinīs, to enter the navel,
through the practice for seven nights, one shall cause even those possessed of vajra-intelligence to fall.
One should perform the meditation-mantra and consume [the substance] of the evil-minded;
at midday or at midnight, one should commence this rite,
naked and with hair disheveled, facing south, and knowing the ritual procedure.
One should recite the mantra of the fire-god while employing the utkūṭāsana posture:
HŪM PHAṬ RAṂ RAṂ RAṂ [Name of] such-and-such person who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution RAṂ RAṂ RAṂ HŪM PHAṬ.
By this mere recitation on the fourteenth day for a full day and night,
even if Vajradhara himself were to die [in one's presence], there is no doubt about it.
Having performed the pacification rite (*śāntika*) for him alone, if there is freedom from evil, [the result follows].
Through the recitation of this great mantra, peace shall come:
Oṃ svāhā a āḥ vaṃ! May [Name] become free from evil; may there be peace for him alone! Vaṃ aṃ aḥ oṃ svāhā.
Subsisting on milk, wearing white garments, with a peaceful mind,
dwelling in emptiness, his body smeared with white unguents;
[he offered] meats to crows, dogs, cats, and mongooses.
One should devour and kill them all; there is no need for deliberation in this matter.
The sixty-fourth chapter, the Unveiling of the Union of Vajrabhairava, the Lord of Wrathful Deities, from the Abhidhānottara.
